Title: Instances of vampires in Lasombra's TWDA

Messages.Author: Dawnfire
Messages.Body:
Hello there.

I have this mental disorder that makes me interested in doing all
sorts of databases and statistics, just for my own fun. During a
longish time, I put together a simple Excel-file where all vampires
currently in the game are sorted in their clans and inside the clans,
sorted by their occurrence - I've counted how many copies of each can
be found in all of Lasombra's tournament winning decks in the archive.
The list is in format: name - # of copies - Cap - group

It's up to date as of this writing, 7th Aug 2009.

If no one finds any use for it, that's fine - but in the case someone
wants to take a look of it, the excel file is here for free use
however you like:

http://rapidshare.de/files/48058566/VTES_vamp_TWDA_count.xls.html

In case you do want to take a look or use it for something, you should
take account of a few things - Firstly, the vampires are directly
comparable only to others in their own group. Group 1 has been usable
far longer than group 5, so group 1 (and 2) are massively over-
represented in numbers compared to how good they are versus the later
ones.
Secondly, It's not an absolute guarantee that a vampire is good or
usable if it appears x times - as someone has pointed out here once,
TWDA has decks that shouldn't be there (in the respect of their
quality), and it's impossible to tell if some vampires are there as
"proxies" or as emotional attachment, not by logical evaluation.
Thirdly, typoing has been taken into accord as well as I could - each
vampire was searchd for both with accents in name and without (e.g
Dónal and Donal) and some spelling errors I figured might happen have
also been considered (e.g Ehrich Weiss and Erich Weiss). Regardless,
theer are bound to be some counting errors and some missed typoes - I
only used my head, and if someone typoed Cardano as Cargano in their
lists, it is most likely not accounted for.

Well, except that I would argue that this information contradicts the
idea that the rules for contestation provide disincentive to play the
popular/powerful vampires. 'Cause:

A) The popular/powerful vampires are the ones that show up most in the
TWDA.

B) That the popular/powerful vampires show up the most in the TWDA, it
means that they win a lot, meaning they probably don't get contested
that often.

It seems, looking at this data, that there is likely no reason at all
to consider "will I contest my important powerful popular vampires"
when deciding a deck to play at a tournament.

-Peter

A third factor to consider: large vampires tend to appear in larger
numbers in crypts, even thought the player plans to bring only one
copy into play. This is because the cost of multiples is reduced for
large vampires. A player running 10-caps is less likely to aspire to
getting as many as 4 minions into play.

No.

The penalty for having a contestable card in your uncontrolled region that
someone else had in play could be "instant game loss" and it would still provide
no more deterrent to playing popular/powerful vampires. There are simply too
many good vampires in the game to meaningfully use that as a deck-building
criteria, and even if one did, that quickly turns into "I know that you know
that I know that you know...", which renders the whole thing even less
applicable in practice.
